sentences.c: 北冥有鱼，其名为鲲。
sentences.m: 北海有一条鱼，名字叫鲲。
sentences.e: In the Northern Sea there is a fish, and its name is Kun.

sentences.c: 鲲之大，不知其几千里也。
sentences.m: 鲲非常大，不知道它有几千里长。
sentences.e: The Kun is so huge that no one knows how many thousand li it spans.

sentences.c: 化而为鸟，其名为鹏。
sentences.m: 它变化成鸟，名字叫鹏。
sentences.e: It transforms into a bird, and its name is Peng.

sentences.c: 鹏之背，不知其几千里也；怒而飞，其翼若垂天之云。
sentences.m: 鹏的背，不知道有几千里宽；它奋起而飞，翅膀就像挂在天边的云。
sentences.e: The back of the Peng — no one knows how many thousand li across; when it rouses itself and flies, its wings are like clouds hanging from the edge of the sky.

sentences.c: 是鸟也，海运则将徙于南冥。
sentences.m: 这只鸟，当海水翻腾动荡时，就要迁往南海。
sentences.e: This bird, when the seas heave and move, will migrate to the Southern Sea.

sentences.c: 南冥者，天池也。
sentences.m: 南海，是天然形成的大池。
sentences.e: The Southern Sea is the Pool of Heaven.

sentences.c: 齐谐者，志怪者也。
sentences.m: 《齐谐》这本书，是记载怪异之事的。
sentences.e: The Qi Xie is a book that records strange things.

sentences.c: 谐之言曰：「鹏之徙于南冥也，水击三千里，抟扶摇而上者九万里，去以六月息者也。」
sentences.m: 《齐谐》上说：「鹏迁往南海时，翅膀拍击水面激起三千里的波涛，乘着盘旋而上的旋风飞上九万里的高空，是凭借六月的大风而离开的。」
sentences.e: The Qi Xie says: "When the Peng migrates to the Southern Sea, it beats the water for three thousand li, mounts the whirling wind and rises ninety thousand li, departing on the breath of the sixth month."

sentences.c: 野马也，尘埃也，生物之以息相吹也。
sentences.m: 山野中的雾气、空中的尘埃，都是生物用气息吹拂的结果。
sentences.e: The wild horses of the marsh, the dust in the air — these are what living things blow forth with their breath.

sentences.c: 天之苍苍，其正色邪？其远而无所至极邪？
sentences.m: 天色苍苍茫茫，这是它真正的颜色吗？还是因为太远而看不到尽头呢？
sentences.e: Is the blue of the sky its true color, or is it simply so far away that there is no end to it?

sentences.c: 其视下也，亦若是则已矣。
sentences.m: 鹏从高空往下看，也不过就像这样罢了。
sentences.e: When the Peng looks down from that height, it is just like this as well.

sentences.c: 且夫水之积也不厚，则其负大舟也无力。
sentences.m: 况且水积得不深，就没有力量承载大船。
sentences.e: Moreover, if water is not piled deep enough, it has no strength to bear a great ship.

sentences.c: 覆杯水于坳堂之上，则芥为之舟；置杯焉则胶，水浅而舟大也。
sentences.m: 在堂前低洼处倒一杯水，放根小草就当船；放上杯子就粘住浮不起来，这是水太浅而船太大的缘故。
sentences.e: Pour a cup of water into a hollow in the hall, and a mustard seed will float as a boat; set the cup down and it sticks fast — the water is too shallow and the boat too large.

sentences.c: 风之积也不厚，则其负大翼也无力。
sentences.m: 风的积聚如果不厚重，就没有力量托负巨大的翅膀。
sentences.e: If the wind is not piled deep enough, it has no strength to bear the great wings.

sentences.c: 故九万里则风斯在下矣，而后乃今培风；背负青天而莫之夭阏者，而后乃今将图南。
sentences.m: 所以鹏飞上九万里的高空，风就在它下面了，然后才乘着风力；背靠着青天而没有什么能阻挡它，然后才打算往南飞。
sentences.e: So at ninety thousand li the wind lies beneath it, and only then does it ride the wind; with the blue sky on its back and nothing to block it, only then does it set its course southward.

sentences.c: 蜩与学鸠笑之曰：「我决起而飞，抢榆枋而止，时则不至，而控于地而已矣，奚以之九万里而南为？」
sentences.m: 蝉和斑鸠讥笑它说：「我们一下子起飞，碰到榆树、檀树就停下来，有时飞不到，落到地上就是了，何必飞上九万里往南去呢？」
sentences.e: The cicada and the young dove laughed at it, saying: "We take off in a rush and stop at the elm or the sandalwood; sometimes we don't even make it and simply drop to the ground. Why go ninety thousand li to the south?"

sentences.c: 适莽苍者，三餐而反，腹犹果然；适百里者，宿舂粮；适千里者，三月聚粮。
sentences.m: 到近郊去的人，只带三餐的饭，回来时肚子还是饱的；到百里之外去的人，前一天就要舂米备粮；到千里之外去的人，要用三个月来聚集干粮。
sentences.e: One who goes to the near countryside takes three meals and comes back with his belly still full; one who goes a hundred li must husk grain the night before; one who goes a thousand li must gather provisions for three months.

sentences.c: 之二虫又何知！
sentences.m: 这两个小虫又懂得什么呢！
sentences.e: What would these two little creatures know!

sentences.c: 小知不及大知，小年不及大年。
sentences.m: 小智比不上大智，短寿比不上长寿。
sentences.e: Small understanding cannot reach great understanding, nor a short span of life a long one.

sentences.c: 奚以知其然也？
sentences.m: 怎么知道是这样呢？
sentences.e: How do we know this is so?

sentences.c: 朝菌不知晦朔，蟪蛄不知春秋，此小年也。
sentences.m: 朝菌不知道一个月的时光，蟪蛄不知道一年的四季，这就是短寿。
sentences.e: The morning mushroom knows nothing of the passing of a month, the cicada knows nothing of spring and autumn — these are the short-lived.

sentences.c: 楚之南有冥灵者，以五百岁为春，五百岁为秋；上古有大椿者，以八千岁为春，八千岁为秋，此大年也。
sentences.m: 楚国南边有一种叫冥灵的树，把五百年当作春天，五百年当作秋天；上古有一种叫大椿的树，把八千年当作春天，八千年当作秋天，这就是长寿。
sentences.e: South of Chu there is a tree called Mingling, which takes five hundred years for spring and five hundred for autumn; in high antiquity there was the Great Chun, which took eight thousand years for spring and eight thousand for autumn — these are the long-lived.

sentences.c: 而彭祖乃今以久特闻，众人匹之，不亦悲乎！
sentences.m: 而彭祖至今以长寿独闻名于世，一般人都想和他相比，岂不可悲吗！
sentences.e: Yet Pengzu alone is famed today for his long life, and everyone wants to match him — is that not pitiful!

sentences.c: 汤之问棘也是已。
sentences.m: 商汤问棘的话，也是这样说的。
sentences.e: So it was also with Tang's questioning of Ji.

sentences.c: 穷发之北有冥海者，天池也。
sentences.m: 不毛之地的北面有个大海，是天然的大池。
sentences.e: North of the barren land there is a dark sea, the Pool of Heaven.

sentences.c: 有鱼焉，其广数千里，未有知其修者，其名为鲲。
sentences.m: 那里有一条鱼，宽几千里，没有人知道它有多长，名字叫鲲。
sentences.e: There is a fish there, several thousand li broad, and no one knows its length; its name is Kun.

sentences.c: 有鸟焉，其名为鹏，背若太山，翼若垂天之云，抟扶摇羊角而上者九万里，绝云气，负青天，然后图南，且适南冥也。
sentences.m: 那里有一只鸟，名字叫鹏，背像泰山，翅膀像挂在天边的云，乘着旋风盘旋而上九万里，穿过云层，背负青天，然后打算往南飞，将要到南海去。
sentences.e: There is a bird there, named Peng, whose back is like Mount Tai and whose wings are like clouds hanging from the edge of the sky; it mounts the whirlwind and spirals up ninety thousand li, cuts through the clouds, bears the blue sky on its back, and then sets its course south, bound for the Southern Sea.

sentences.c: 斥鴳笑之曰：「彼且奚适也？我腾跃而上，不过数仞而下，翱翔蓬蒿之间，此亦飞之至也，而彼且奚适也？」
sentences.m: 小池泽里的鹌鹑讥笑它说：「它要到哪里去呢？我腾跃而起，不过几丈高就落下来，在蓬蒿之间盘旋，这也算飞到极致了。可它究竟要到哪里去呢？」
sentences.e: The quail of the marsh laughed at it: "Where is it going? I leap up and at most a few fathoms high I come down again, wheeling among the fleabane and wormwood — that is the utmost of flying. So where is it going?"

sentences.c: 此小大之辩也。
sentences.m: 这就是小和大的区别。
sentences.e: Such is the distinction between the small and the great.

sentences.c: 故夫知效一官，行比一乡，德合一君，而征一国者，其自视也亦若此矣。
sentences.m: 所以那些才智足以胜任一官之职、品行能联合一乡之人、德行能合于一君之心、能力能取信于一国之人的人，他们看待自己，也就像这只鹌鹑一样。
sentences.e: So those whose wisdom fits them for one office, whose conduct wins over one village, whose virtue satisfies one ruler, whose ability earns the trust of one state — they look at themselves much as that quail did.

sentences.c: 而宋荣子犹然笑之。
sentences.m: 而宋荣子却讥笑他们。
sentences.e: And Song Rongzi laughed at them all the same.

sentences.c: 且举世而誉之而不加劝，举世而非之而不加沮，定乎内外之分，辩乎荣辱之境，斯已矣。
sentences.m: 而且世上的人都称赞他，他也不会因此更加努力；世上的人都非议他，他也不会因此更加沮丧。他认定了内我和外物的分别，辨明了荣辱的界限，如此而已。
sentences.e: The whole world praises him and he is not spurred on; the whole world blames him and he is not cast down. He has settled the line between inner and outer, and marked out the boundary of honor and shame — and that is all.

sentences.c: 彼其于世未数数然也。
sentences.m: 他对于世俗的东西，并不急切追求。
sentences.e: Toward the world he is not eager or grasping.

sentences.c: 虽然，犹有未树也。
sentences.m: 即使这样，他还是有没能树立起来的东西。
sentences.e: Still, there is something he has not yet established.

sentences.c: 夫列子御风而行，泠然善也，旬有五日而后反。
sentences.m: 列子驾着风飞行，轻快美妙，十五天之后才返回。
sentences.e: Liezi rode the wind and went light and well, returning only after fifteen days.

sentences.c: 彼于致福者，未数数然也。
sentences.m: 他对于求福的事，并不急切追求。
sentences.e: He was not eager after blessings either.

sentences.c: 此虽免乎行，犹有所待者也。
sentences.m: 这样虽然免于步行，还是有所凭借的。
sentences.e: Though he escaped walking, he still had something to depend on.

sentences.c: 若夫乘天地之正，而御六气之辩，以游无穷者，彼且恶乎待哉！
sentences.m: 至于顺应天地的本性，驾驭六气的变化，遨游于无穷境界的人，他还依赖什么呢！
sentences.e: But one who rides the true nature of heaven and earth, drives the changes of the six breaths, and wanders in the infinite — what would he need to depend on!

sentences.c: 故曰：至人无己，神人无功，圣人无名。
sentences.m: 所以说：至人没有自我，神人没有功业，圣人没有名声。
sentences.e: Therefore it is said: the Perfect Man has no self, the Holy Man no merit, the Sage no name.
